title: Redwood discovery - reliability & incident tolerance with HelixCommerce
summary: Discovery focused on HelixCommerce reliability needs for real-time recommendations and checkout flows. Discussed hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, multi-region routing, fallbacks to smaller models, SLA targets, and security requirements. Agreed next steps: send pricing/security pack, schedule POC for Dedicated baseline and runbench in EU + US, and share runbook template.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rahul Desai (Redwood SE), Lina Morales (Helix CTO), Samir Patel (Helix Platform), Grace Lee (Helix Ops)
Meeting ID: ff-20260325-helix-8421

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
00:05 - Lina: Hi, Lina Morales, CTO at HelixCommerce. We've got Samir and Grace with me.
00:08 - Samir: Samir Patel, platform engineer; looking at inference infra for recommendations and checkout fraud checks.
00:12 - Grace: Grace Lee, ops, responsible for SRE and incident response.
00:16 - Maya: Awesome. I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood, and Rahul's our SE. We'll focus on reliability and incident tolerance for Hosted/Dedicated/Private options.
00:22 - Rahul: Hi all. Quick agenda: understand your SLOs, current infra, failure modes, and what fallback policies you expect. Also cover multi-region and SLA expectations.
00:30 - Lina: Great. Quick context: we run real-time recs at checkout, latency sensitive. 99.9% of requests need <120ms p95. We're currently on a mix of in-house TF models for recs and a managed vendor for embeddings; looking to consolidate.
00:45 - Samir: Traffic spikes Black Friday-ish, but daily QPS is usually 800-1,200, peaks up to 6k. We need predictable throughput and predictable tail latency.
00:55 - Grace: Our main concern is incidents: vendor outages or region failures. We need graceful degradation and clear runbooks.
01:05 - Maya: Okay that helps. In Redwood we support Hosted (fast to start), Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For reliability, primary levers are multi-region routing, model variants + fallback policies, and prefix/KV cache to reduce load.
01:20 - Rahul: On model fallbacks: you can define routing policies so critical endpoints route to Dedicated GPUs in primary region, with a fallback to a cheaper model variant or smaller quantized model in another region. That preserves availability, albeit with potential quality change.
01:40 - Lina: How do you manage consistency? If we fallback in EU to a smaller model, we might see recommendation drift.
01:48 - Rahul: Good point. We recommend a two-tier policy: first fallback to a compatible variant (same weights, different quantization) to preserve behavior. Second tier is smaller architecture only for read-only non-critical flows. We also support canary rollouts to measure drift before full switch.
02:05 - Samir: Is KV cache region-aware? If we failover from us-west to europe-west, what about cached prefixes?
02:12 - Rahul: KV cache is per-cluster by default. For multi-region, we have cache-coherency strategies: either independent per-region caches (fast, simple) or an optional global TTL-synced cache. Global cache adds latency and complexity, so many customers accept per-region caches and warm the target region during failover.
02:32 - Grace: Warm how? Is that an automated warm-up?
02:35 - Rahul: We expose APIs to pre-warm popular prefixes and prefetch KV entries. For Dedicated customers we can coordinate warm-up using traffic mirroring or synthetic hits as part of the runbook.
02:45 - Lina: SLA. You mentioned Dedicated can have SLA-backed uptime/latency. What do those SLAs look like?
02:52 - Maya: For Dedicated we offer contractual uptime targets (e.g., 99.9% availability) and latency SLOs based on configured pool sizes. Hosted has a best-effort SLO and credits, but not the same contractual SLA as Dedicated. Private can be customized depending on deployment and support package.
03:05 - Samir: If there's an outage in our primary region, do you automatically reroute to another region? How long does that take?
03:12 - Rahul: Our smart routing can detect regional health via active probes and metrics. Failover time depends on policy: automatic failover can be 30-90s for routing changes plus model warm-up; prewarmed standby reduces that to under 10s for stateless models. We recommend automated failover for non-sensitive flows and manual/controlled for critical flows unless you prewarm.
03:40 - Grace: During failover, how do you handle in-flight requests? Any retries or error patterns?
03:45 - Rahul: We support graceful retry policies. For streaming responses, we can attempt reconnects; for request/response we have idempotency keys and automatic retries with exponential backoff. We also expose per-request diagnostics so you can see if a request failed due to capacity or region errors.
04:00 - Lina: Security/regulatory: we need EU data residency for EU customers. Hosted options in EU region acceptable, but we may prefer Private for some EU-only data. What's the story for audit logs and KMS?
04:12 - Maya: Dedicated and Hosted both support region isolation; Private gives you full control. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management, and provide audit logs with retention add-ons. We'll share SOC2+ISO docs in the security pack.
04:25 - Samir: About cost: running prewarmed multi-region pools seems expensive. What are cost controls?
04:30 - Rahul: You can use burst pools and autoscale; we also recommend hybrid routing—keep a small prewarmed Dedicated cluster in secondary region for critical endpoints, and use Hosted or smaller variants for low-criticality traffic. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching profiles to reduce cost.
04:50 - Lina: Can we do routing by percent? Like 95% traffic to primary, 5% to secondary as part of DR tests?
04:56 - Rahul: Yes, percent-based routing and canary splits are first-class. You can also route by attribute (user region, endpoint criticality) or cost tier.
05:05 - Grace: On runbooks: if primary region has a total outage, will Redwood provide an incident support playbook and an SRE contact?
05:11 - Maya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we provide a runbook and an escalation path with on-call contacts. For Hosted we provide status pages and support SLAs per plan. We'll include the runbook template in the POC package.
05:25 - Samir: Any limitations for stateful KV? Our recs service uses user session state sometimes.
05:30 - Rahul: We try to keep inference stateless; session-ish state should be passed as part of the prompt. For larger state we recommend external session store with latency-conscious read patterns. Internal KV cache is optimized for model key-value cache, not long lived session DB.
05:48 - Lina: For the POC we want a benchmark: p50/p95 p99, error rate under load, failover time, model quality delta when falling back. Can Redwood run that in US + EU?
05:58 - Rahul: Yes. We'll run a two-region benchmark with synthetic traffic and mirrored real traffic if you want. We'll measure latencies, QPS, and quality delta using your holdout prompts. We'll include scripted failover to validate warm-up.
06:12 - Grace: Any known gotchas?
06:15 - Rahul: A few: cross-region cold starts are the biggest source of added latency; prefix cache misses on region switch; and model variant drift if you fall back to a different architecture. We mitigate with prewarm, compatible quant variants, and canary tests.
06:30 - Lina: Sounds reasonable. Last question: what's the typical timeline to go from POC to Dedicated production?
06:35 - Maya: Usually 4-8 weeks if infra and security checks are quick. Private deployments can add lead time for networking & HSM integrations. We'll size a Dedicated pool based on your QPS and SLO targets during the POC.
06:50 - Samir: Okay next steps?
06:53 - Maya: I'll send pricing + security pack by Friday. Rahul will send the POC plan. Helix to share traffic patterns and holdout prompts. We'll propose a POC kickoff week of April 6.
06:59 - Lina: Agreed. Thanks everyone.
07:02 - Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up via email with links to docs and the benchmark spreadsheet.
07:06 - (Call ends)
